terra.problem: David's title as king of Israel is a fact from outside this passage and needs a supporting reference.
1 Kings 17:1 introduces Elijah but does not identify him as a prophet. The claim needs a reference that does, such as 1 Kings 18:22.
David's kingship is not stated in this passage and needs a supporting reference.
Solomon's relationship to David and his kingship are not stated in this passage and need supporting references.
Solomon being David's son is not stated in this passage and needs a supporting reference.
Acts 7:47 does not establish that Solomon was David's son or that the house was in Jerusalem. Those outside facts need supporting references.
The verse says the Most High does not dwell in houses made by human hands. Saying He doesn't live in what people build broadens that beyond houses.
Solomon had not just built the house. Stephen had just mentioned its construction.
Pharaoh's appearance in Stephen's earlier account is outside this passage and needs its own reference, such as Acts 7:10.
“No jokes on this one” comments on how Papa is telling the passage.
“Stephen wasn't going for friendly” assigns him an unstated intention without marking it as Papa's guess.
Abraham's appearance at the opening of Stephen's account is outside this passage. Genesis 12:1 does not support that claim; Acts 7:2–3 does.
“They didn't want one more word” assigns the council an unstated desire.
The text says they covered their ears, but it does not establish that they heard nothing at all.
“I'll just say it plainly” comments on how Papa is telling the passage.
The text says Saul was there, but does not say he was standing.
“The mourning came from other people” assumes the God-fearing men were distinct from all the council members. The text does not establish that.
